0.long_answer: Cyclopia, also referred to as synophthalmia or alobar holoprosencephaly, is an extremely rare and life-threatening congenital disorder. It results from a severe developmental defect where the embryonic forebrain fails to divide into the two hemispheres, leading to the formation of a single central eye or partially fused eyes. A hallmark feature of cyclopia is the presence of a non-functional or absent nose, sometimes replaced by a proboscis, which is an abnormal tubular structure. Due to the profound developmental abnormalities, most cases result in miscarriages or the birth of non-viable infants. The condition is named after the Cyclops of Greek mythology, who were one-eyed giants.
